content: Isoniazid, a medication used to treat and prevent tuberculosis (TB), may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the BCG vaccine. If you are using the liquid form of this medication, be aware that it may contain sugar. This is particularly important for individuals with diabetes or conditions requiring sugar restriction. Use caution and consult your doctor if this applies to you. During pregnancy, isoniazid should only be used when absolutely necessary, as determined by your healthcare provider. While this medication does pass into breast milk, it is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. However, always discuss with your doctor before use. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of isoniazid or increase the risk of serious side effects. It is essential to maintain a list of all medications and supplements you are taking, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal products, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may also interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as urine glucose tests, potentially leading to false results. In the event of an overdose, seek immediate medical attention. If the individual has severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). For non-emergency cases, contact a poison control center (1-800-222-1222 in the U.S. or 1-844-764-7669 in Canada). While taking isoniazid, regular laboratory and medical tests, such as sputum tests, liver and kidney function tests, and complete blood counts, are necessary to monitor your condition and detect any potential side effects. Ensure you attend all scheduled medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose of isoniazid, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. For those on a weekly dosing schedule, consult your doctor or pharmacist if you miss a dose and are unsure how to proceed. Store isoniazid at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and do not flush it down the toilet or pour it into a drain unless instructed to do so. Isoniazid has been associated with rare but serious liver disease, which can be fatal. The risk is higher in individuals over 35 years old, those who consume alcohol or use illegal injection drugs, and those with pre-existing liver conditions. Your doctor should monitor your liver function with regular tests while you are on this medication. This antibiotic is effective only against bacterial infections and will not work for viral infections such as the common cold or flu. It is crucial to take isoniazid on an empty stomach, either one hour before or two hours after meals, as directed by your doctor. If using the liquid form, measure the dose carefully with a proper measuring device or spoon. For optimal results, take isoniazid at evenly spaced intervals. If prescribed daily, take it at the same time each day. If prescribed weekly, take it on the same day(s) and at the same time each week. Continue taking the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve, to ensure the infection is completely treated. Your doctor may recommend taking vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) alongside isoniazid to prevent certain side effects, such as nerve problems. Be aware that isoniazid may interact with foods containing tyramine or histamine, such as cheese, red wine, and certain fish, potentially causing symptoms like high blood pressure, skin flushing, headache, dizziness, or a rapid heartbeat. Notify your doctor immediately if these symptoms occur. A special diet may be recommended while taking this medication. Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, or stomach upset. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks. Serious allergic reactions to isoniazid are rare but possible. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor promptly. This information is not exhaustive and does not replace professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about isoniazid and your specific health needs.
